name: Fix RBAC that grants the wrong access
objective: CKS › Cluster + System Hardening (15% + 15%). Drill EVERY hardening corner harder than the exam on a real multi-node kind cluster: control-plane manifest perms, kubelet read-only port + anonymous-auth + authz mode, two apiserver admission/flag hardenings, least-privilege RBAC, ServiceAccount token hardening, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. questions.title: Diagnose & fix: RBAC that grants the wrong access
questions.teach:
When `kubectl auth can-i` says `no` for something a SA should have, the fault is usually a wrong `resources`, `verbs`, or `apiGroups` entry in the **Role**. Inspect with `kubectl -n cks-learn get role <r> -o yaml` and compare each rule to what's required.

**Gotcha:** fix the existing Role, don't create a second one — and keep it least-privilege: grant exactly what's needed, nothing more.
questions.prompt:
In `cks-learn`, SA `audit-sa` is bound (via RoleBinding `audit-rb` → Role `audit-role`) but it still **cannot** `list pods` — the Role was seeded pointing at the wrong resource. Diagnose and fix the Role so `audit-sa` can `get,list` pods, without granting write access. Don't delete and rebuild from scratch — find and fix what's wrong.

Target: SA `audit-sa` can `list pods` (`yes`) but cannot `delete pods` (`no`) in `cks-learn`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n cks-learn get role audit-role -o yaml` — its rule lists the wrong `resources` (not `pods`). `kubectl -n cks-learn edit role audit-role` and set `resources: ["pods"]` with `verbs: ["get","list"]`.
questions.solution:
# describe/get shows audit-role grants get,list on 'services' instead of 'pods'
kubectl -n cks-learn patch role audit-role --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/rules/0/resources","value":["pods"]}]'
kubectl auth can-i list pods   --as=system:serviceaccount:cks-learn:audit-sa -n cks-learn   # yes
kubectl auth can-i delete pods --as=system:serviceaccount:cks-learn:audit-sa -n cks-learn   # no

verification.description: SA audit-sa can list pods but cannot delete pods in cks-learn (Role fault fixed)

questions.eli5:
Picture a keycard (`audit-sa`) that's *supposed* to open the **Pods room** but keeps getting rejected at the door. The wiring looks right — there's a Role (`audit-role`), and a RoleBinding (`audit-rb`) stapling it to the keycard — yet `kubectl auth can-i list pods` still says **`no`**. So where's the bug?

Nine times out of ten, when the binding exists but access is denied, the mistake is *inside the Role's rule*: it's pointing at the **wrong resource** (or wrong verbs, or wrong apiGroup). Here the Role was seeded to grant access to **services** instead of **pods** — so the card opens a door, just not the one you wanted.

The way to solve it is to **look, don't guess**: `kubectl -n cks-learn get role audit-role -o yaml` and read the rule. You'll see `resources: ["services"]` where it should say `["pods"]`. Fix *that existing rule* — don't build a brand-new Role beside it.

And keep it tight: grant exactly `get,list` on `pods`, nothing more — no `delete`, no wildcards. The goal is `list pods = yes`, `delete pods = no`.

**Watch out for:**

- **Fix the existing Role, don't make a second one.** Adding a new Role/binding alongside the broken one is messy and not what's asked.
- **Inspect before editing** — `get role ... -o yaml` tells you the real fault (wrong `resources`, `verbs`, or `apiGroups`). Don't blind-fire.
- **Stay least-privilege.** Grant only `get,list` on `pods`; adding `delete` or `*` would make `delete pods` return `yes` and fail the goal.
- **A RoleBinding's target (`roleRef`) can't be changed** — but here the binding is fine; it's the Role's rule that's wrong, and Roles *are* editable.
- **Verify both directions**: `list pods = yes` AND `delete pods = no`, using `--as=system:serviceaccount:cks-learn:audit-sa`.
questions.deepDive:
## Diagnose & fix: RBAC that grants the wrong access — full rundown

### Mental model
This is an RBAC **debugging** drill. A ServiceAccount is bound to a Role but `kubectl auth can-i` returns `no` for an action it should have. When the **binding exists** yet access is denied, the fault is almost always inside the **Role's rule**: a wrong `resources`, `verbs`, or `apiGroups` entry. The method is: inspect → identify the mismatched field → patch the *existing* Role (don't rebuild) → re-verify, keeping it least-privilege.

### RBAC decision chain — where it can break
```
SA identity  ──►  RoleBinding (subjects + roleRef)  ──►  Role (rules: apiGroups × resources × verbs)
```
| Symptom | Likely broken link |
|---|---|
| `can-i` = no, **no binding** found | missing/incorrect RoleBinding (subject or roleRef) |
| `can-i` = no, binding **exists** | Role rule wrong: `resources`, `verbs`, or `apiGroups` |
| works in wrong namespace only | Role/RoleBinding in the wrong namespace |
| cluster resource denied | needs ClusterRole + (Cluster)RoleBinding |

Here the binding is correct; the Role rule points at the wrong `resources` (`services` instead of `pods`).

### Diagnose
```bash
# read the Role's rules
kubectl -n cks-learn get role audit-role -o yaml
# look at rules[0]: resources: ["services"]  <-- should be ["pods"]

# confirm the binding is actually wired to the SA
kubectl -n cks-learn get rolebinding audit-rb -o yaml
#   roleRef -> Role/audit-role ; subjects -> ServiceAccount cks-learn/audit-sa

# reproduce the failure
kubectl auth can-i list pods --as=system:serviceaccount:cks-learn:audit-sa -n cks-learn   # no
```

### Fix the existing Role (don't recreate)
```bash
# surgical JSON patch of the resources field
kubectl -n cks-learn patch role audit-role --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/rules/0/resources","value":["pods"]}]'

# ensure verbs are get,list (patch if the seed had them wrong too)
# kubectl -n cks-learn patch role audit-role --type=json \
#   -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/rules/0/verbs","value":["get","list"]}]'
```
Or interactively: `kubectl -n cks-learn edit role audit-role` and set
```yaml
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]           # core group for pods
  resources: ["pods"]
  verbs: ["get","list"]
```

### Verify both directions
```bash
kubectl auth can-i list   pods --as=system:serviceaccount:cks-learn:audit-sa -n cks-learn   # yes
kubectl auth can-i delete pods --as=system:serviceaccount:cks-learn:audit-sa -n cks-learn   # no
```

### Common Role-rule faults
| Field | Wrong | Right (for pods read) |
|---|---|---|
| `resources` | `["services"]` | `["pods"]` |
| `verbs` | `["get"]` (can't list) | `["get","list"]` |
| `apiGroups` | `["apps"]` | `[""]` (core) |
| resource name | `["pod"]` | `["pods"]` (plural) |

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Fix the existing Role; don't add a second one.** The task says diagnose-and-repair, and extra objects muddy least privilege.
- **Inspect before editing** — `get -o yaml` reveals the exact wrong field; guessing wastes time.
- **Keep least-privilege.** Grant only `get,list` on `pods`; adding `delete`/`*` makes `delete pods = yes` and fails the goal.
- **`roleRef` is immutable** on a binding — good thing the binding is fine here; only the Role needs editing (Roles are mutable).
- **Plural, lowercase resource names** (`pods`), correct `apiGroups` (`""` for core).
- **Test as the SA** with `--as=system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<name>` and check **both** the allowed and the forbidden verb.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n cks-learn get role audit-role -o yaml           # find the wrong field
kubectl -n cks-learn patch role audit-role --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/rules/0/resources","value":["pods"]}]'
kubectl auth can-i list   pods --as=system:serviceaccount:cks-learn:audit-sa -n cks-learn   # yes
kubectl auth can-i delete pods --as=system:serviceaccount:cks-learn:audit-sa -n cks-learn   # no
```
